PARKS, ARTS & CULTURE COMMITTEE 
DRAFT Meeting Minutes – September 1, 2026 
This content was translated & edited with the assistance of AI. The content has been reviewed and verified to be accurate and 
complete, and represents the intent of Mary Danko, PACC Admin. 
 
Call to Order 
The meeting was called to order at approximately 12:02 PM after initial technical 
difficulties with audio and Zoom connectivity. Chair Councilor Schachter confirmed all 
attendees could hear and participate. 
Attendance 
Committee Members Present: 
• Chair Councilor Allie Schachter 
• Councilor Becca Brown McKnight (remote) 
• Councilor Carter Neubieser (remote) 
City Staff and Participants: 
• City Attorney Office representatives ((including City Attorney Brown (Zoom) and 
Attorney Emmett Wood) 
• Burlington Parks, Recreation & Waterfront, Parks & Central Facilities Division Director, 
Deryk Roach 
• Burlington Community and Economic Development Office leadership (CEDO) Directory 
Kara Alnasrawi & Samantha McGinnis (CSMP) 
• Burlington City Arts Director Doreen Kraft 
• CAO Katherine Schad 
Approval of Minutes 
A motion to approve the minutes of the previous meeting was made by Councilor McKnight 
and seconded by Chair Schachter. The motion passed unanimously.
Public Comment Summary 
Public comment opened at approximately 12:03 PM. Several members participated both in 
person and via Zoom.  
Sheltering on Public Lands Policy Briefing 
Attorney Wood gave a comprehensive overview of the City’s Shelter on Public Lands policy, 
including its origins in the settlement agreement resulting from the Croteau v. Burlington 
lawsuit. Key points included: 
• Background on Fourth, Eighth, and Fourteenth Amendment claims raised in the 
lawsuit. 
• Requirements for due process, including consistent notice and storage of personal 
property. 
• Clarification that camping is prohibited across City parks and public lands, aside from 
staffed campgrounds. 
• Explanation of triage procedures used due to staffing constraints, distinguishing 
environmental hazards, safety concerns, and general encampments. 
• Importance of consistency in enforcement to avoid creating implied property rights or 
permissive conditions. 
Committee Questions & Discussion 
Committee members engaged in an extensive discussion focused on resource 
constraints, enforcement consistency, and long-term strategies. Key discussion points 
included: 
• Need for increased staffing for Parks, DPW, and outreach teams. 
• Clarification that the City cannot restrict rights granted in the existing policy without 
ACLU approval. 
• Acknowledgment of the significant statewide components of homelessness, addiction, 
and mental health systems. 
• Consideration of temporary sanctioned camping areas and legal implications for City 
liability. 
• Recognition of the need for improved communication between Council and 
Administration. 
• Public advocacy suggestions related to state-level funding and policy changes.
Closing & Adjournment 
Public comment was closed at 12:38 PM. The meeting adjourned at approximately 1:30 
PM. Chair Schachter thanked all attendees for their participation and noted that the next 
meeting will continue pending agenda items not reached during this session.
